chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Kulayb al-Saydawi, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) gave a sermon and said: "Every intoxicant is forbidden."'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on intoxicants according to the Prophet's sermon?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith cites the Prophet’s sermon declaring every intoxicant (*kull muskir*) as forbidden, establishing the foundational principle for the prohibition of *khamr*. This broad definition (*kull muskir*) extends the ruling beyond wine to all substances causing intoxication, a key distinction in Shia fiqh for deriving rulings on new intoxicants. The narration underscores the divine origin of this prohibition, linking the legal ruling directly to the Prophet’s authoritative declaration.
